description: Route and worker-batch performance budgets, keyed on METHOD /path (exact OpenAPI path template). Each entry declares the maximum database-call count, downstream-call count, response bytes, application latency and memory for one operation. Measured fields are populated by src/scripts/measure-route-budgets.mjs from a real measurement and are null until then. check-route-budgets.mjs validates structure, enforces every populated measurement against its ceiling, and reports coverage as a fraction of the whole route surface — never as a bare pass.

surface.criticalSelection: A route is critical when it is (a) issued on every authenticated page load, (b) the primary list or detail read of an in-scope module, (c) the primary transactional write of an in-scope module, or (d) a scheduled worker batch that iterates tenant data. Everything outside that set is declared-out-of-scope, not measured-and-passing.
surface.honesty: totalOperations is recomputed from openapi.json on every gate run. The value stored here is the count at the release commit; the gate prints the live number so the denominator can never go stale without being visible.

read-path-explain.what: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of the route's dominant read, run as the non-BYPASSRLS app role with app.organization_id set.
read-path-explain.caveat: Buffer blocks are environment-independent and are the number that ratchets. The millisecond percentiles are taken on loopback Postgres, so they exclude pool wait and network round trip and are a LOWER BOUND on production latency — they are never written into measuredLatencyP95Ms, which is the end-to-end application ceiling and stays unmeasured until an HTTP-level harness fills it.

db-call-count.what: QueryTelemetryTracker statement count around a real service/route invocation (src/db/query-telemetry.ts).

measurement.commitNote: HEAD at the moment the numbers were taken. The commit that RECORDS them is its child, since writing the manifest is itself a change — re-run this script after any commit that alters a measured route so the recorded commit stays the one the numbers describe.
